h1: The 8 Best Desktop Monitor Privacy Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight 24 inch desktop monitor privacy options, from 2-pack filters to a built-in filter monitor, compared on fit and price.
summary: The Peslv 2-pack is the best desktop privacy screen for matched dual-monitor desks, with a removable filter and identical coverage on both screens. The magnetic 2-pack wins if you toggle privacy often. Single-monitor desks should look at the SightPro, and the ViewSonic VG2448-PF only makes sense if you need a new monitor anyway.
intro: Most privacy filter regrets come from one boring mistake: the buyer matched the diagonal and ignored the aspect ratio. A 24 inch panel can be 16:9 or 16:10, and a filter cut for the wrong one leaves a visible strip of exposed screen or hangs off the edge. Every filter in this ranking is cut for a 24 inch, 16:9 monitor, so check your own spec sheet before anything else.

We reviewed eight options on their listings: seven add-on filters, mostly sold in pairs, and one monitor with a filter built in. Our data covers size, aspect ratio, pack count and attachment style, not viewing angle or brightness loss, so we rank on fit, convenience and cost per screen and leave the optics claims to the makers.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: A removable 2-pack for matched dual-monitor desks.
products.description:
The Peslv sells two removable filters cut for 24 inch, 16:9 monitors, in the $50 to $100 range. Buying a matched pair matters more than it sounds: two filters from the same batch give both screens the same tint and the same viewing cutoff, so a dual setup does not look patchy from the side. A removable design also means you can take the filter off for color-critical work.

It leads because it combines that matched pair with the plainest, most predictable fit in the group. The magnetic pack below costs the same but depends on your bezel, and the IPROKKO costs less but leaves the attachment unlisted. Pairing certainty is what puts the Peslv first.

Buy it for two identical 24 inch screens. The caveat is price: it runs above the $25 to $50 pairs, and it fits only 24 inch 16:9, so a single monitor wastes the second filter.

products.name: 2 Pack 24 Inch Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen for Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.verdict: Magnetic attachment for quick on and off.
products.description:
This magnetic 2-pack covers 24 inch, 16:9 monitors in the $50 to $100 range, and the attachment is the entire point. Magnets let you pull a filter off in a second when a colleague needs to see the screen, then snap it back for the train or the open office. Slide-in or adhesive-style mounts make that routine tedious enough that people stop doing it.

It lands second because the Peslv matches its price and size without a mounting condition. A magnetic filter needs something for the magnets to grip, and that is the catch the listing leaves to you.

Pick it if you present or pair-work often and want privacy that is easy to switch off. Check that your monitor's bezel can hold the magnets cleanly before ordering. If you never share your screen, the extra convenience buys you nothing.

products.name: IPROKKO [2-Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Widescreen Monitor
products.verdict: A 2-pack listed as compatible with multiple monitor brands.
products.description:
The IPROKKO is a 2-pack of 24 inch, 16:9 filters in the $25 to $50 range, and it is the only pack here whose listing states multi-brand compatibility. That claim has real value in an office where one desk has a Dell, the next an HP and a third something older, because a filter that only fits one bezel design becomes a drawer of orphans.

It ranks third because it undercuts the Peslv and the magnetic pack by a full price bracket while still delivering a pair. What holds it back is information. The listing never names the attachment method, so you are buying a pair without knowing how it mounts.

It suits mixed-brand offices and cost-conscious dual-monitor desks. Read the full listing and owner questions about mounting first, since that is the unknown here.
products.skipIf: You want a stated magnetic mount.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A single 24 inch filter for one-monitor desks.
products.description:
SightPro sells one 24 inch, 16:9 filter in the $25 to $50 range, built for the desk with one monitor. Single-unit packs matter because a 2-pack is only a bargain if you use both filters. For a lone screen, a pair leaves you paying for a spare you will never mount.

It ranks fourth because it is the better-defined single option, but the format limits it. Two SightPros for a dual desk cost more than the Peslv or magnetic 2-pack, which defeats the point. Its pros are simplicity and a low entry price, and nothing in its data suggests extra features.

Buy it for one 24 inch, 16:9 display. The caveat is the unlisted attachment style, so confirm how it mounts before you commit, particularly if your bezel is thin.

products.name: Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Monitor
products.description:
The Magicmoon is a 24 inch, 16:9 2-pack in the $25 to $50 range, aimed at dual-monitor desks that cannot justify the $50 to $100 packs. Two filters at this price brings the per-screen cost down to the level of a single filter elsewhere, which is the whole case for it.

It sits fifth because the listing is thin. Attachment and compatibility are not stated, while the IPROKKO at the same price at least names multi-brand fit. When two products share a price and size, the one that tells you more about itself gets the higher rank, and here that is the IPROKKO.

Choose it for a budget dual desk where you can verify the mounting method in owner questions. If you want documented specs before spending anything, move up the list.

products.name: [2 Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Widescreen Monitor
products.verdict: A plain 2-pack of 24 inch widescreen filters.
products.description:
This unbranded-style 2-pack covers 24 inch, 16:9 widescreen monitors and sits in the $50 to $100 range. It is a plain pair of filters with nothing in the listing to separate it from the competition, which is exactly why it ranks mid-table.

Price is the problem. The Peslv charges the same and gives you a defined removable design, and the magnetic pack gives you quick toggling. This one gives you less information for the same money, so it only competes when the price drops. Against the IPROKKO and Magicmoon in the $25 to $50 bracket, paying double for fewer details is hard to defend.

Buy it only if you find it discounted below the Peslv. Otherwise the pricier bracket and sparse specs push it down. Fit still depends on a 24 inch, 16:9 panel.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 24 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: A budget single filter for one 24 inch monitor.
products.description:
This is a single 24 inch, 16:9 privacy filter in the $25 to $50 range, the cheapest way to cover one monitor in this ranking. It exists for the buyer who wants a basic screen filter and nothing else, with no pair to split or spare to store.

It ranks seventh because the SightPro matches it on size and price bracket while the listing here names even less. With equal prices, the more documented product wins, and that is the SightPro. The simple buy and low cost keep it above the ViewSonic, which solves a different problem.

Buy it for a budget single-monitor desk where you only need basic visual privacy. The caveat is the sparse listing: attachment style is not stated, so confirm it before ordering and make sure your panel is truly 16:9.

products.name: ViewSonic VG2448-PF 24 Inch IPS 1080p Ergonomic Monitor with Built-In Privacy Filter
products.verdict: A monitor with a built-in toggleable privacy filter.
products.description:
The ViewSonic VG2448-PF is a different product: a 24 inch IPS 1080p monitor with a privacy filter built into the display, in the $200 to $500 range. The filter toggles on and off, so there is no sticky film and no hunting for a mount. It also brings HDMI, DisplayPort and USB inputs and a 40 degree tilt range.

It ranks last as a privacy fix because it replaces your monitor instead of covering it. Every filter above does the job for a fraction of the cost, and none of them require you to retire a working display. The built-in design removes fit risk entirely, but you pay for that certainty.

Buy it if your current screen is due for replacement and you want privacy switchable from the monitor. Anyone keeping their existing display should buy a filter instead.

whatMatters.detail: A privacy filter is cut to a specific diagonal and aspect ratio, and a mismatch leaves exposed screen or overhang. A 24 inch 16:9 filter will not sit correctly on a 24 inch 16:10 panel. Look up your monitor's exact resolution or aspect ratio in its manual, then match it to the filter listing before ordering. Never trust the diagonal alone.

Pack count decides cost per screen. A 2-pack like the Peslv or Magicmoon usually costs less than two singles, but it only pays off if you have two matching monitors. A single like the SightPro suits one screen. Count your displays, confirm they share a size, and buy the pack that matches. Mismatched monitors need separate singles.

Attachment controls how often you will actually use the filter. Magnetic mounts come on and off in seconds, which matters when you share your screen. Other removable designs are slower, so people leave them on. Check the listing for the mounting method, and if it is missing, as with the IPROKKO, ask the seller before buying.

Compatibility covers whether the mount works with your bezel. The IPROKKO lists multi-brand fit, which helps in mixed offices. Magnetic packs need a surface the magnets can hold. Check your monitor's bezel width and material, then confirm the listing names your brand or a universal fit before you buy.

A built-in filter, like the ViewSonic VG2448-PF's toggle, removes fit and mounting concerns but means buying a monitor. The add-on filters cost a fraction of that. It only pays when you need a new display anyway. Compare the $200 to $500 monitor against a $25 to $100 filter on a screen you already own.

faq.a: Only if your monitor is 24 inch and 16:9. Every filter here is cut for that size, and the ViewSonic VG2448-PF is a monitor, not a filter. Check your display's spec sheet against the listing before ordering the Peslv or any other pack.

Ignoring aspect ratio. Many 24 inch panels exist, and a 16:9 filter on a 16:10 screen leaves gaps or an off-center fit. Measure or look up your resolution first, because the Peslv, IPROKKO and the rest are all cut for 16:9.

faq.q: Is the ViewSonic worth it over a filter?
faq.a: Only when you need a new monitor anyway. The ViewSonic VG2448-PF sits in the $200 to $500 bracket and toggles its filter on and off, while the Peslv pair costs $50 to $100 and covers two screens you already own.

faq.q: How do I install a filter?
faq.a: Follow the maker's steps for the attachment style. The magnetic 2-pack is listed as magnetic and snaps on, while the Peslv is removable. The IPROKKO and Magicmoon do not state a method, so read the listing before you order.

Use a soft, dry or lightly damp cloth and avoid harsh chemicals that can mar the filter surface. Magnetic filters like the second-place pack come off easily, which makes cleaning both the filter and the monitor simpler.

Our data does not cover brightness impact, so we make no claim. Filters of this kind generally reduce the light reaching you, so check owner feedback on the Peslv or magnetic pack before assuming the screen will look unchanged.

finalTake: Buy the Peslv pair if you run two matching 24 inch, 16:9 monitors, or the magnetic pack if you share your screen often. One monitor means a single filter, and the ViewSonic is for people already replacing their display. Confirm size and aspect ratio before ordering, because fit is the one thing a filter cannot forgive.
